timeline.text_full: I'm brainstorming improvement ideas across the four projects, starting with the crypto trading bot: tracking actual slippage instead of leaving it null, and expanding exit reason categories beyond just stop_loss for richer analytics. For coachvision, I'm weighing footage generation and idle-alerting ideas but finding they overlap with existing closed issues, so I'm considering something more distinct like scheduled calendar reminders for training sessions to reduce idle periods. For the UFC dashboard, I'm thinking about tracking closing line value against past movement alerts to see how well they predicted actual outcomes. I'm also considering cost/budget tracking for LLM API usage in the Overseer pipeline itself, and a time-to-ship metric distinct from the existing attention score. Now I'm narrowing down to a shortlist across projects, starting with slippage tracking for the crypto bot to measure execution quality by comparing actual fills to signal prices, and expanding exit-reason categorization since the current taxonomy doesn't yet distinguish trailing stops from time-based exits. For coachvision, I'm considering an automatic footage quality/completeness check before processing, rejecting bad clips early on resolution, duration, or lighting issues, since a proactive calendar-reminder idea felt too similar to the existing idle-escalation feature. For the UFC dashboard, I'm exploring closing-line-value backtest tracking that correlates line-movement alerts with actual fight outcomes to validate whether the alerts are useful signals. For Overseer, I'm weighing an LLM/API token-usage and cost-tracking widget per run to monitor pipeline operating costs, distinct from the attention score idea, versus adding retry/backoff logic for individual read-tool failures so partial data doesn't block the weekly digest. timeline.text_full: The CLV idea, though scoring below the duplicate threshold, is essentially the same core concept as #68's already-shipped CLV tracking with sharp/square flagging—I should either meaningfully differentiate it by focusing on correlating CLV with actual fight outcomes to measure predictive accuracy, or drop it entirely. Since the verdict was "similar" not "duplicate," propose_enhancement won't require an extends field, but I'll include extends: 68 anyway to be transparent that this builds on the existing feature, framing my contribution as outcome-validation rather than just pattern-flagging. I need to check the slippage idea too, since it seems similar to already-shipped #23 which logs per-signal rejection reasons and fill slippage. Actually, the null slippage_bps in telemetry is probably just because recent decisions are all holds with no actual trades, not a gap in the #23 implementation. That means the slippage idea is essentially a duplicate, so I should drop it and think of a different crypto-related feature not already covered by open issues like #65 or basic optimization scheduling. I notice there's per-asset PnL attribution already shipped (#51), but no equivalent breakdown by strategy/account sleeve (breakout, long_short, regime, trend) even though by_account unrealized PnL data exists. That seems like a solid new idea worth checking for duplicates, while exit_reasons taxonomy, coachvision quality gate, and overseer token cost all look clear to keep as-is.

systemic_risk.message: coachvision, Trading bot are all showing risk signals in the same run. That many independently-run projects going wrong at once is more likely one shared cause — a cloud runner outage, an expired API key, a billing lapse — than several unrelated problems. Worth checking for that before triaging each one separately.
